title: Formal Resurgence and Differential Transcendence in Lean 4 (stokes-vandermonde)
description: Lean 4 formalization of the Borel–Stokes–Vandermonde criterion and machine-checked proofs of differential transcendence across spectral geometry, analytic number theory, combinatorics, special functions, and mathematical physics. Version 3.3.0 adds four new kernel-verified modules (12,380 new lines) and three standalone audit ledgers: (1) 3D and 2D compact hyperbolic Selberg–Stokes–Vandermonde theorems proving strong C({t}) differential transcendence of geodesic von Mangoldt OGFs and formal Borel–Laplace series plus C{1/u} and C(u) Laplace ADE obstructions given the explicit analytic input packages CompactHyperbolic3DSelbergData (pure-polynomial reflection +(Vol/pi) xi^2 with zero trivial zeros) and CompactHyperbolicSelbergData (requiring zero eigenvalue-simplicity or additional spectral-spacing assumptions; no concrete hyperbolic manifold is instantiated in Lean yet); (2) on the standard closed-form Cartan compact rank-1 symmetric space (CROSS) spectral-multiplicity quasipolynomials and heat sums (not derived from Riemannian manifolds in Lean): bosonic Euler-product odd-sphere / odd-dimension uniqueness over C(q), strong C({t}) wave-EGF D-transcendence across S^{2r}, CP^n, HP^n, OP^2, ADE spherical 3-manifold (S^3/I*, O*, T*, D*_m) formal Molien reciprocity and even parity (oddPart = 0, borelAmp = 0), and unconditional C(t) heat-trace D-transcendence for every even-dimensional simply connected CROSS via P(-d/dt) reduction to baseHeatInt and baseHeatHalf; and (3) elementary RH/GRH-independent strong C({t}) differential transcendence and Laplace ADE obstructions for prime von Mangoldt moment series driven by the trivial zeros of riemannZeta at both asymmetric s_0 = 2 (literal convergent Dirichlet moments (-1)^n sum Lambda(m)(log m)^n / m^2) and s_0 = 1/2 (G_Lambda). All 169 audited declarations depend strictly on standard Lean axioms ([propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound] or subsets thereof) and pass independent leanchecker --fresh replay. Prime-number-theorem inputs use MediumPNT from PrimeNumberTheoremAnd (PNT+) by Alex Kontorovich, Terence Tao, and contributors. Google Gemini, OpenAI Codex, and Anthropic Claude assisted with exploration, auditing, drafting, and Lean formalization.
